key_insight: UEval is a focused benchmark of 1,000 expert‑curated questions that require models to generate both images and text, and it exposes how simple LLM‑as‑judge approaches miss important multimodal subtleties.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a standardized, fine‑grained evaluation for unified multimodal generators (models that must produce coherent image+text outputs) and the challenge of reliably assessing open‑ended multimodal quality.
method: Curated a 1,000‑item dataset of questions drawn from 8 real‑world tasks, each requiring joint image and text output.
Designed questions to span diverse reasoning types (step‑by‑step guides, textbook explanations, visual reasoning, design/layout, etc.) to test multimodal capabilities.
Proposed an evaluation protocol that goes beyond naive LLM‑as‑judge setups to better capture multimodal correctness and subtle failure modes (e.g., mismatched visuals, incomplete explanations).
impact: UEval gives researchers and practitioners a targeted, realistic benchmark to compare and improve unified multimodal models, and highlights evaluation blind spots so metrics and human/automated judging can be improved.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: unified model input → joint image + text output → multimodal evaluator (human/automated)
Example card: one question with the expected image and accompanying explanatory text side‑by‑side
Bar chart: benchmark performance across several baseline unified models showing gaps in visual vs. textual quality
Infographic showing distribution of the 8 task categories and reasoning types covered
paper_title: UEval: A Benchmark for Unified Multimodal Generation
paper_authors: Bo Li, Yida Yin, Wenhao Chai, Xingyu Fu, Zhuang Liu
